bio_en: Sako of Sev Kar was one of the early ARF fighters of the 1890s colony in Persia that included Karo Zorian, Nikol Duman, Hovnan Davtian and Galust Aloyan. A memoirist who met him about 1894 describes a black-bearded, sturdy villager of gentle, democratic character and selfless devotion. Andranik later told how Sako, posing as a cattle merchant, outfaced the moneylender Jezayir agha of Kizil-Aghaj. Sako died in his sick bed in late 1908, and his widow Mariam Tsovianian wrote from Tiflis asking that his memory be honoured with education for the poor.
